question: The Latin term 'corpus delicti' literally means 'body of the deceased' and in forensic law refers to the physical corpse of the victim.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually FALSE. Corpus delicti (from Latin) means 'body of the crime' — the sum of evidence that a criminal act took place. It is not synonymous with 'corpse.' A murder conviction can theoretically rest on corpus delicti even without a body if other evidence establishes that the crime occurred.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Corpus delicti means 'body of the crime' (the totality of evidence that a crime occurred), NOT the physical body of the deceased. Confusing the two is one of the most common errors in forensic medicolegal documentation.
